To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the community structure of brain networks has a clear hierarchical organization, (ii) the community structure at a given scale is related to the temporal scale of information flow at that same level, and (iii) the community structure in brain networks is shaped by physical proximity.

we propose an algorithm that detects communities in networks at different scales by using information flow and that we find a hierarchical repertoire of community structure in the anatomical and functional connectomes of macaque and human brain.
the information flow in a brain network is characterized by oscillations with a wide range of temporal scales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of communities and their hierarchical organization in complex networks.
the detection of community structure in brain networks.
the identification and analysis of community structure in brain networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain is a complex system in which the community organization is hierarchical and the information is propagated at different scales.

the community structure of the brain network is a natural consequence of the brain's functional organization and that it is shaped by physical proximity, functional specialization, and the temporal scale of the information flow.

the community structure of a brain network can be seen as a hierarchical organization of communities, which in turn are defined by the different temporal scales at which information is exchanged in the network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
communities are not static structures but dynamic, evolving in time, and their dynamics are governed by the information flow.
the community structure in the brain network can be naturally understood as a hierarchical repertoire of spatial and temporal scales of information processing.

the brain's information processing is organized in communities of nodes with similar function and/or spatial proximity that communicate with each other in a hierarchical fashion, in which each scale of the hierarchical structure has its own temporal scale for information processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community structure of a brain graph is a function of its topology, the information flow it supports and its hierarchical organization.
the brain network is not a static object, but rather it can be understood as a dynamic entity that is constantly changing its structure.
the information flow in a network may constitute a natural and effective way to define communities at different scales.
